answer: Each agent locks a bond in escrow before claiming any work. Auditors chosen at random re-run a hidden sample of its outputs. If results match, the bond returns with a fee. If results are fabricated, the bond goes to the auditors. A sybil operator must post a separate bond for each identity, and every cheating identity burns its own stake, so mass registration costs more than it earns. Sampling stays unpredictable, like a falcon riding a ridge of wind, and bond sizes are public, so each claim shows its capital like pigment in plain view.
